subject: maths
title: Primary 5 Discount, GST and Annual Interest
seo_title: P5 Discount, GST and Interest Worksheets: Free Primary 5 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Finding discount, GST and annual interest
meta_desc: Free P5 maths practice on percentage: discount and sale price, 9% GST, receipts and annual interest. 100 questions with answers and bar models.
key_big: Take the discount off the usual price first, then add 9% GST on the sale price.
key_sub: 20% off $45: discount $9, sale price $36. GST: 9% of $36 = $3.24, so you pay $39.24.
body_html:
Discount

A discount is an amount taken off the usual price. It is a percentage of the usual price. Sale price = usual price − discount.

Example 1

The usual price of a school bag is $45. It is sold at a 20% discount. Find the sale price.

Discount: 20% of $45 = 20/100 × $45 = $9. Sale price: $45 − $9 = $36.

Answer: $36

GST

In Singapore, GST (Goods and Services Tax) is 9%. It is added to the price. Price after GST = price before GST + 9% of the price before GST.

Example 2

An item costs $80 before GST. Find the price after 9% GST.

GST: 9% of $80 = 9/100 × $80 = $7.20. Price after GST: $80 + $7.20 = $87.20.

Answer: $87.20

Discount, then GST

When an item is on sale, take off the discount first. GST is worked out on the sale price, the price you actually pay.

Annual interest

A bank pays interest on your savings. “Per annum” means for each year. The interest for 1 year is a percentage of the money saved. The amount in the bank after 1 year = money saved + interest.

Example 3

Siti saves $5000 in a bank at 2% interest per annum. How much is in her account after 1 year?

Interest: 2% of $5000 = 2/100 × $5000 = $100. Amount: $5000 + $100 = $5100.

Answer: $5100

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
20% off $45 = $45 − $20 = $25Find 20% of $45 ($9), then subtract: $36
Adding the discount: $45 + $9 = $54A discount is taken away: $45 − $9 = $36
GST on the usual price after a discountWork out 9% of the sale price
Adding $9 for 9% GST9% GST on $80 is 9/100 × $80 = $7.20
Giving $5100 as the interestThe interest is $100; $5100 is the amount in the bank

faq.q: What is taught in P5 percentage?
faq.a: Primary 5 students learn to write a part of a whole as a percentage and to find a percentage of an amount. They use this to find discount, GST and annual interest, as in the MOE syllabus.

faq.q: How do I calculate GST in Singapore?
faq.a: GST in Singapore is 9%, so find 9% of the price and add it: 9% GST on $80 is $7.20, and the price after GST is $87.20. If there is a discount, take it off first and work out GST on the sale price.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with discount?
faq.a: The most common mistake is subtracting the percentage as dollars, for example 20% off $45 as $45 − $20 = $25. Find 20% of $45 first ($9), then subtract to get the sale price of $36.

faq.q: How do I explain annual interest to my child?
faq.a: Tell your child that the bank pays a percentage of the money saved for each year it stays there. $5000 at 2% per annum earns $100 interest in 1 year, so the account then has $5100.

items.q: The usual price of a school bag is $45. It is sold at a 20% discount. How much is the discount?
items.e: 10% of $45 = $4.50, so 20% = 2 × $4.50 = $9. ($20 uses the percentage as dollars; $36 is the sale price.)

items.q: The usual price of a school bag is $45. It is sold at a 20% discount. What is the sale price?
items.e: Discount: 20% of $45 = $9. Sale price: $45 − $9 = $36. ($25 subtracts 20 dollars, not 20%; $54 adds the discount.)

items.q: A pair of shoes costs $60. There is a 10% discount. How much is the discount?
items.e: 10% of $60 = $60 ÷ 10 = $6. ($10 uses the percentage as dollars; $54 is the sale price.)

items.q: A pair of shoes costs $60. There is a 10% discount. What is the sale price?
items.e: Discount: 10% of $60 = $6. Sale price: $60 − $6 = $54. ($50 subtracts $10; $66 adds the discount.)

items.q: A T-shirt costs $38. It is sold at 50% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: 50% is half. $38 ÷ 2 = $19. ($57 adds 50%; $76 doubles instead of halving; $37.50 takes away 50¢, not 50%.)

items.q: What is the sale price of this rice cooker?
items.e: 25% is one quarter. Discount: $64 ÷ 4 = $16. Sale price: $64 − $16 = $48. ($39 subtracts 25 dollars; $16 is the discount.)

items.q: A standing fan costs $120. It is sold at a 5% discount. How much is the discount?
items.e: 10% of $120 = $12, so 5% = $12 ÷ 2 = $6. ($5 uses the percentage as dollars; $12 is 10%; $114 is the sale price.)

items.q: An item is sold at a 20% discount. Which gives the sale price?
items.e: The usual price is 100%. Take away 20%: 100% − 20% = 80%. So the sale price is 80% of the usual price. 20% of the usual price is only the discount.

items.q: A bicycle helmet costs $90. It is sold at a 30% discount. What is the sale price?
items.e: 10% of $90 = $9, so 30% = $27. Sale price: $90 − $27 = $63. ($60 subtracts 30 dollars; $27 is the discount.)

items.q: A pair of sports shoes costs $80. It is sold at a 15% discount. What is the sale price?
items.e: 10% of $80 = $8 and 5% = $4, so 15% = $12. Sale price: $80 − $12 = $68. ($65 subtracts 15 dollars; $92 adds the discount.)

items.q: A set of storybooks costs $35. It is sold at a 40% discount. What is the sale price?
The usual price of a lamp is $50. Mrs Lim gets a discount of $10. What percentage discount is this?
items.e: Discount as a fraction of the usual price: 10/50 = 20/100 = 20%. (10% uses the dollars as the percentage; 80% is the part she pays; 5% comes from 50 ÷ 10.)

items.q: The usual price of a jacket is $80. The sale price is $60. What percentage discount is given?
items.e: Discount: $80 − $60 = $20. Compare with the usual price: 20/80 = 1/4 = 25%. (20% uses the dollars; 75% is the part paid; 33⅓% divides by the sale price.)

items.q: The usual price of a water bottle is $40. The sale price is $34. What percentage discount is given?
items.e: Discount: $40 − $34 = $6. 6/40 = 15/100 = 15%. (6% uses the dollars; 85% is the part paid; 34% uses the sale price.)

items.q: A study desk costs $250. It is sold at a 12% discount. What is the sale price?
items.e: 1% of $250 = $2.50, so 12% = 12 × $2.50 = $30. Sale price: $250 − $30 = $220. ($238 subtracts 12 dollars; $30 is the discount.)

items.q: A laptop costs $1200. It is sold at a 15% discount. What is the sale price?
items.e: 10% of $1200 = $120 and 5% = $60, so 15% = $180. Sale price: $1200 − $180 = $1020. ($1185 subtracts 15 dollars; $1380 adds the discount.)

items.q: A pair of shoes costs $72. Zhi Hao buys it at a 25% discount. How much does he save?
items.e: The amount saved is the discount. 25% of $72 = $72 ÷ 4 = $18. ($54 is what he pays; $47 is $72 − 25.)

items.q: A T-shirt costs $15. A shop gives 10% off the total when you buy 2. How much do 2 T-shirts cost?
items.e: Total: 2 × $15 = $30. Discount: 10% of $30 = $3. Pay: $30 − $3 = $27. ($20 subtracts $10; $28.50 takes 10% off one T-shirt only; $3 is the discount.)

items.q: The usual price of a toy is $56. It is sold at a 25% discount. Use the model to find the sale price.
items.e: 25% = 1/4, so the bar has 4 units. 4 units = $56, 1 unit = $56 ÷ 4 = $14. Sale price = 3 units = 3 × $14 = $42. ($31 subtracts 25 dollars; $14 is the discount.)

items.q: A bag costs $80. The shop gives a 20% discount first. Then Mdm Wong uses a $5 voucher. How much does she pay?
items.e: 20% of $80 = $16, so the sale price is $64. Voucher: $64 − $5 = $59. ($55 subtracts 20 dollars; $60 treats the $5 as 5% more off; $69 adds the voucher.)

items.q: In Singapore, GST is 9%. How much GST is charged on a $100 item?
items.e: 9% of $100 = 9/100 × $100 = $9. ($109 is the price after GST, not the GST.)

items.q: How much is 9% GST on $80?
items.e: 1% of $80 = $0.80, so 9% = 9 × $0.80 = $7.20. ($9 uses the percentage as dollars; $72 is 90% of $80.)

items.q: An item costs $80 before GST. What is the price after 9% GST?
items.e: GST: 9% of $80 = $7.20. Price after GST: $80 + $7.20 = $87.20. ($89 adds $9; $72.80 subtracts the GST; $7.20 is only the GST.)

items.q: How much is 9% GST on $50?
A pair of school shoes costs $25 before GST. How much is the 9% GST?
items.e: 1% of $25 = $0.25, so 9% = 9 × $0.25 = $2.25. ($2.50 is 10%; $27.25 is the price after GST; $9 uses the percentage as dollars.)

items.q: A pair of headphones costs $50 before GST. What is the price after 9% GST?
items.e: GST: 9% of $50 = $4.50. Price after GST: $50 + $4.50 = $54.50. ($59 adds $9; $50.09 adds 9¢; $45.50 subtracts the GST.)

items.q: Which gives the price of an item after 9% GST?
items.e: The price is 100%. GST adds 9% more: 100% + 9% = 109% of the price. 9% of the price is only the GST; 91% takes the GST away.

items.q: A microwave oven costs $200 before GST. What is the price after 9% GST?
items.e: GST: 1% of $200 = $2, so 9% = $18. Price after GST: $200 + $18 = $218. ($209 adds $9; $182 subtracts the GST; $18 is only the GST.)

items.q: A box of art materials costs $30 before GST. What is the price after 9% GST?
How much is 9% GST on $120?
A lunch box costs $15 before GST. What is the price after 9% GST?
A table fan costs $45 before GST. How much does Jun Jie pay after 9% GST?
How much is the GST on this receipt?
items.e: GST is 9% of the subtotal. 1% of $38 = $0.38, so 9% = 9 × $0.38 = $3.42. ($2.25 is GST on the socks only; $3.80 is 10%; $9 uses the percentage as dollars.)

items.q: What is the total on this receipt?
items.e: Total = subtotal + GST = $38.00 + $3.42 = $41.42. ($47 adds $9; $34.58 subtracts the GST; $40.25 adds GST on the socks only.)

items.q: A television costs $1500 before GST. What is the price after 9% GST?
A pencil case costs $28 and a ruler set costs $12, before GST. What is the total price after 9% GST?
items.e: Price before GST: $28 + $12 = $40. GST: 9% of $40 = $3.60. Total: $40 + $3.60 = $43.60. ($42.52 adds GST on the pencil case only; $49 adds $9.)

items.q: The price of a mattress is $70 before GST. What is the price after 9% GST?
items.e: GST: 9% of $70 = $6.30. Price after GST: $70 + $6.30 = $76.30. ($79 adds $9; $77 adds 10%; $63.70 subtracts the GST.)

items.q: An item costs $90 before GST. How much more is its price after 9% GST?
items.e: The difference is the GST: 9% of $90 = 9 × $0.90 = $8.10. ($98.10 is the price after GST; $9 uses the percentage as dollars.)

items.q: Shop A sells a speaker for $50 before GST. Shop B sells the same speaker for $54, GST included. Which shop is cheaper?
items.e: Shop A: $50 + 9% GST = $50 + $4.50 = $54.50. Shop B: $54. Shop B is cheaper by 50¢. (Shop A by $4 forgets to add GST to Shop A’s price.)

items.q: Ali buys 4 cushions at $12 each, before GST. How much does he pay after 9% GST?
items.e: Price before GST: 4 × $12 = $48. GST: 9% of $48 = $4.32. Total: $48 + $4.32 = $52.32. ($13.08 is for 1 cushion only; $57 adds $9; $43.68 subtracts the GST.)

sets.title: Discount, then GST on a receipt

items.q: A $50 bag is sold at a 20% discount. Then 9% GST is added. GST is worked out on which amount?
items.e: You pay GST on the price you actually pay. 20% of $50 = $10, so the sale price is $50 − $10 = $40, and GST is 9% of $40.

items.q: How much is the discount on this receipt?
items.e: 25% of $64 = $64 ÷ 4 = $16. ($25 uses the percentage as dollars; $48 is the sale price.)

items.q: The usual price of a school bag is $45. It is sold at a 20% discount. Then 9% GST is added. How much do you pay?
items.e: Sale price: $45 − $9 = $36. GST: 9% of $36 = $3.24. Pay: $36 + $3.24 = $39.24. ($40.05 adds GST on the usual price; $49.05 forgets the discount; $36 forgets the GST.)

items.q: How much is the GST on this receipt?
items.e: GST is 9% of the sale price: 9% of $60 = 9 × $0.60 = $5.40. ($7.20 is GST on the usual price $80; $1.80 is GST on the discount.)

items.q: What is the total on this receipt?
items.e: Total = sale price + GST = $60.00 + $5.40 = $65.40. ($67.20 adds GST on $80; $87.20 forgets the discount.)

items.q: A jacket costs $100. It is sold at a 10% discount, and 9% GST is added. What is the price after GST?
items.e: Sale price: $100 − $10 = $90. GST: 9% of $90 = $8.10. Price: $90 + $8.10 = $98.10. ($99 adds GST on $100; $109 forgets the discount; $90 forgets the GST.)

items.q: A bicycle costs $200. It is sold at a 15% discount, and 9% GST is added. How much does it cost?
items.e: Discount: 15% of $200 = $30, so the sale price is $170. GST: 9% of $170 = $15.30. Total: $170 + $15.30 = $185.30. ($188 adds GST on $200; $194 subtracts 15 dollars and adds 9 dollars.)

items.q: A pair of shoes costs $60. It is sold at 50% off, and 9% GST is added. What is the price after GST?
items.e: Sale price: half of $60 = $30. GST: 9% of $30 = $2.70. Total: $30 + $2.70 = $32.70. ($35.40 adds GST on $60; $30 forgets the GST; $65.40 forgets the discount.)

items.q: The shop takes 10% off the whole bill. Then 9% GST is added. What is the total?
items.e: Bill: $35 + $25 = $60. Discount: 10% of $60 = $6, so the sale price is $54. GST: 9% of $54 = $4.86. Total: $54 + $4.86 = $58.86. ($59.40 adds GST on $60; $65.40 forgets the discount; $54 forgets the GST.)

items.q: A standing fan costs $120. It is sold at a 20% discount, and 9% GST is added. What is the price after GST?
A school bag costs $75. It is sold at a 40% discount. How much GST is paid on the sale price?
items.e: Discount: 40% of $75 = $30, so the sale price is $45. GST: 9% of $45 = $4.05. ($6.75 is GST on the usual price; $2.70 is GST on the discount.)

items.q: A $50 board game is bought with a $10 voucher. GST is charged on the price after the voucher. What is the total?
items.e: Voucher first: $50 − $10 = $40. GST: 9% of $40 = $3.60. Total: $40 + $3.60 = $43.60. ($44.50 adds GST before using the voucher; $49 adds $9.)

items.q: A pair of goggles and a swim cap cost $90 in all. They are sold at a 30% discount, and 9% GST is added. What is the total?
items.e: Discount: 30% of $90 = $27, so the sale price is $63. GST: 9% of $63 = $5.67. Total: $63 + $5.67 = $68.67. ($71.10 adds GST on $90; $98.10 forgets the discount.)

items.q: A shop gives 20% off and then adds 9% GST. Hafiz says, “I pay 11% less than the usual price.” Is he right?
items.e: Try $100: 20% off gives $80. GST is 9% of $80 = $7.20, not $9. Total: $87.20 for every $100, which is 12.8% less. The GST is worked out on the smaller sale price.

items.q: A study desk costs $250. It is sold at a 20% discount, and 9% GST is added. What is the price after GST?
items.e: Sale price: $250 − $50 = $200. GST: 9% of $200 = $18. Total: $200 + $18 = $218. ($222.50 adds GST on $250; $272.50 forgets the discount.)

items.q: 5 notebooks cost $4 each. The shop gives 10% off the total, and then adds 9% GST. How much do the 5 notebooks cost?
A laptop costs $1500. It is sold at a 10% discount, and 9% GST is added. What is the price after GST?
Kumar buys a $30 storybook at a 10% discount. 9% GST is added. He pays with a $50 note. How much change does he get?
items.e: Sale price: $30 − $3 = $27. GST: 9% of $27 = $2.43. Total: $29.43. Change: $50 − $29.43 = $20.57. ($20.30 uses GST on $30; $23 forgets the GST; $17.30 forgets the discount.)

items.q: Shop A sells a bag for $60 at a 20% discount. Shop B sells the same bag for $50 with no discount. Both shops add 9% GST. Which shop is cheaper?
The usual price of a pair of inline skates is $150. Nurul buys it at a 20% discount, and 9% GST is added. She pays with three $50 notes. How much change does she get?
items.e: Sale price: $150 − $30 = $120. GST: 9% of $120 = $10.80. Total: $130.80. Change: $150 − $130.80 = $19.20. ($16.50 uses GST on $150; $30 forgets the GST; $40.80 subtracts the GST.)

items.q: A bank pays interest of 2% per annum. What does “per annum” mean?
c: Once only, when you open the account
items.e: “Per annum” means for each year. 2% per annum means the bank pays 2% of your savings for each year.

items.q: Ali puts $5000 in a bank. The interest rate is 2% per annum. How much interest does he get after 1 year?
items.e: 1% of $5000 = $50, so 2% = $100. ($5100 is the amount in the bank, not the interest; $1000 is 20%.)

items.q: Ali puts $5000 in a bank at 2% interest per annum. How much is in his account after 1 year?
items.e: Interest: 2% of $5000 = $100. Amount after 1 year: $5000 + $100 = $5100. ($100 is only the interest; $5002 adds $2; $4900 subtracts the interest.)

items.q: $1000 is saved in a bank at 3% interest per annum. How much interest is earned in 1 year?
items.e: 1% of $1000 = $10, so 3% = $30. ($3 uses the percentage as dollars; $1030 is the amount in the bank.)

items.q: $2000 is saved in a bank at 1% interest per annum. How much interest is earned in 1 year?
$800 is saved in a bank at 5% interest per annum. How much is in the account after 1 year?
items.e: Interest: 10% of $800 = $80, so 5% = $40. Amount: $800 + $40 = $840. ($40 is only the interest; $805 adds $5; $760 subtracts the interest.)

items.q: $3000 is saved in a bank at 2.5% interest per annum. How much interest is earned in 1 year?
$4000 is saved at 3% interest per annum. Which gives the interest for 1 year?
items.e: The interest for 1 year is 3% of $4000 = $120. 103% of $4000 = $4120 is the amount in the bank, not the interest.

items.q: $6000 is saved in a bank at 1.5% interest per annum. How much interest is earned in 1 year?
Mrs Ng puts $10 000 in a bank at 2% interest per annum. How much is in her account after 1 year?
How much interest is earned in 1 year?
How much is in the account after 1 year?
items.e: Interest: 1% of $1200 = $12, so 3% = $36. Amount: $1200 + $36 = $1236. ($36 is only the interest; $1560 adds 30%.)

items.q: $4000 earns $80 interest in 1 year. What is the interest rate per annum?
items.e: 1% of $4000 = $40. $80 is 2 × $40, so the rate is 2% per annum. (80% uses the dollars; 50% comes from $4000 ÷ $80.)

items.q: Ryan has $3000 to save. Bank A pays 2% per annum. Bank B pays 1.5% per annum. How much more interest does Bank A pay in 1 year?
items.e: Bank A: 2% of $3000 = $60. Bank B: 1.5% of $3000 = $45. Difference: $60 − $45 = $15. ($0.50 subtracts the rates as dollars; $60 is Bank A’s interest.)

items.q: Mr Rahman saves $8000 at 2.5% interest per annum. How much is in his account after 1 year?
Kavya’s account had $1500 at the start of the year and $1530 at the end. No money was added or taken out. What is the interest rate per annum?
items.e: Interest: $1530 − $1500 = $30. 1% of $1500 = $15, and $30 = 2 × $15, so the rate is 2%. (30% uses the dollars; 50% comes from $1500 ÷ $30; 20% is 10 times too big.)

items.q: Chloe puts $2000 in Bank A at 2% per annum and $3000 in Bank B at 3% per annum. How much interest does she get in 1 year altogether?
items.e: Bank A: 2% of $2000 = $40. Bank B: 3% of $3000 = $90. Total: $40 + $90 = $130. ($125 uses 2.5% on $5000; $250 uses 5% on $5000; $5130 is the total amount in the banks.)

items.q: $20 000 is kept in a fixed deposit at 3% interest per annum. How much interest is earned in 1 year?
items.e: 1% of $20 000 = $200, so 3% = $600. ($6000 is 30%; $20 600 is the amount, not the interest.)

items.q: Mr Tan borrows $5000 from a bank at 4% interest per annum. How much must he pay back after 1 year?
items.e: When you borrow, you pay back the loan plus interest. Interest: 4% of $5000 = $200. Pay back: $5000 + $200 = $5200. ($200 is only the interest; $4800 subtracts it.)

items.q: Ahmad saves $2400 at 2.5% interest per annum. He hopes to have $2500 after 1 year. How much less than $2500 will he have?
items.e: Interest: 1% of $2400 = $24, so 2.5% = $60. Amount: $2400 + $60 = $2460. Less than $2500 by $2500 − $2460 = $40. ($100 forgets the interest; $60 is the interest; $2460 is the amount.)

items.q: A box of mandarin oranges costs $35 before Chinese New Year. During a sale, it is sold at a 20% discount. What is the sale price?
items.e: 20% = 1/5, so the bar has 5 units. 5 units = $35, 1 unit = $7. Sale price = 4 units = 4 × $7 = $28. ($15 subtracts 20 dollars; $7 is the discount; $42 adds it.)

items.q: Ethan buys a pair of roller skates. The usual price is $84. He gets a 25% discount. How much does he pay?
items.e: 25% = 1/4, so the bar has 4 units. 4 units = $84, 1 unit = $21. He pays 3 units = 3 × $21 = $63. ($59 subtracts 25 dollars; $21 is the discount.)

items.q: Shop A sells a bag at $60 with 25% off. Shop B sells the same bag at $52 with 10% off. Which shop is cheaper?
items.e: Shop A: $60 − $15 = $45. Shop B: $52 − $5.20 = $46.80. Shop A is cheaper by $1.80. (Shop A by $7 subtracts the percentages as dollars: $35 and $42.)

items.q: A bag costs $80. Siti can use either a 30% discount or a $25 voucher, not both. Which is the better deal?
items.e: 30% of $80 = $24, so 30% off gives $56. The voucher gives $80 − $25 = $55. The $25 voucher is better by $1. (30% off by $5 compares 30 with 25.)

items.q: During a National Day sale, everything is 15% off. Mei Ling buys a pair of shoes at $40 and a bag at $60. How much does she pay?
items.e: Total: $40 + $60 = $100. Discount: 15% of $100 = $15. Pay: $100 − $15 = $85. ($70 takes $15 off each item; $15 is the discount; $115 adds it.)

items.q: Xin Yi puts $3000 in a bank at 2% interest per annum. After 1 year, the interest is added, and then she puts in another $500. How much is in the account now?
items.e: Interest: 2% of $3000 = $60, so after 1 year there is $3060. Add $500: $3060 + $500 = $3560. ($3570 gives interest on the $500 too, but it was put in after the year; $3060 forgets the $500.)

items.q: Raju has $100. He buys a $75 video game at a 20% discount, and 9% GST is added. How much money does he have left?
items.e: Sale price: $75 − $15 = $60. GST: 9% of $60 = $5.40. Total: $65.40. Left: $100 − $65.40 = $34.60. ($40 forgets the GST; $25 forgets the discount and the GST; $18.25 forgets the discount.)

items.q: Mrs Lim buys an air purifier at a year-end sale. The usual price is $240. It is sold at a 25% discount, and 9% GST is added. How much does she pay?
items.e: Sale price: $240 − $60 = $180. GST: 9% of $180 = $16.20. Total: $180 + $16.20 = $196.20. ($201.60 adds GST on $240; $261.60 forgets the discount; $180 forgets the GST.)

items.q: Hui Min has $5000. Bank A pays 2% interest per annum. Bank B pays 1.8% per annum. How much more interest does Bank A pay in 1 year?
items.e: Bank A: 2% of $5000 = $100. Bank B: 1.8% of $5000 = $90. Difference: $10. Or: 0.2% of $5000 = $10. ($0.20 subtracts the rates as dollars; $100 is Bank A’s interest.)

items.q: A pair of shoes costs $60 and a cap costs $40. The shoes are 10% off and the cap is 25% off. How much does Priya save on both?
items.e: Shoes: 10% of $60 = $6. Cap: 25% of $40 = $10. Saved: $6 + $10 = $16. ($35 adds the percentages as dollars; $19 swaps the two percentages; $84 is the amount paid.)

items.q: A school bag costs $90. The shop takes 10% off first. Then a $5 voucher is used. How much is paid?
items.e: 10 units = $90, 1 unit = $9. Sale price: 9 units = $81. Voucher: $81 − $5 = $76. ($75 subtracts 10 dollars; $76.50 uses the voucher first; $86 forgets the 10% off.)

items.q: Devi’s family buys 4 tickets to a school concert at $25 each. They get a 10% discount on the total. How much do they pay?
items.e: Total: 4 × $25 = $100. Discount: 10% of $100 = $10. Pay: $100 − $10 = $90. ($97.50 takes 10% off one ticket only; $60 takes $10 off each ticket; $10 is the discount.)

items.q: Two shirts cost $30 each. Shop A: buy 1, get the second at 50% off. Shop B: 20% off both shirts. Which shop is cheaper?
items.e: Shop A: $30 + $15 = $45. Shop B: 20% of $60 = $12 off, so $48. Shop A is cheaper by $3. ($15 is only the discount on the second shirt.)

items.q: A sports shop sells a jersey for $48. Members get 25% off. Non-members get 10% off. How much more does a non-member pay?
items.e: Member: $48 − $12 = $36. Non-member: $48 − $4.80 = $43.20. Difference: $43.20 − $36 = $7.20. Or: 15% of $48 = $7.20. ($15 uses the percentages as dollars; $36 and $43.20 are the two prices.)

items.q: At a book fair, a $25 storybook is sold for $20. What percentage discount does Arjun get?
items.e: Discount: $25 − $20 = $5. Compare with the usual price: 5/25 = 20/100 = 20%. (5% uses the dollars; 25% divides by the sale price $20; 80% is the part paid.)

items.q: Mr Rahman buys 3 shirts at $45 each for Hari Raya Puasa. He gets 20% off the total, and 9% GST is added. How much does he pay?
Wei Ming’s mother can buy a vacuum cleaner online for $120 plus 9% GST, or in a shop for $135 with GST included and 5% off. Which is cheaper?
items.e: Online: $120 + $10.80 GST = $130.80. Shop: 5% of $135 = $6.75 off, so $128.25. $130.80 − $128.25 = $2.55, so the shop is cheaper by $2.55. (Online by $8.25 forgets the GST.)

items.q: Mdm Wong buys 3 bowls of laksa at $6 each and 3 cups of bubble tea at $7 each, before GST. How much does she pay after 9% GST?
items.e: Food: 3 × $6 = $18. Drinks: 3 × $7 = $21. Total before GST: $39. GST: 9% of $39 = $3.51. Pay: $39 + $3.51 = $42.51. ($48 adds $9; $40.89 adds GST on the drinks only; $35.49 subtracts the GST.)

items.q: Sarah has $1200 in a bank at 2% interest per annum. After 1 year, she takes out money to buy a $150 bicycle at a 20% discount, with 9% GST added. How much is left in the bank?
items.e: After 1 year: $1200 + 2% of $1200 = $1200 + $24 = $1224. Bicycle: $150 − $30 = $120, and $120 + $10.80 GST = $130.80. Left: $1224 − $130.80 = $1093.20. ($1069.20 forgets the interest; $1074 forgets the discount and the GST; $1080 forgets the interest and the GST.)

items.q: Farah’s father wants a $1800 television. Shop A gives 15% off. Shop B gives $250 off. Both shops then add 9% GST. Which shop is cheaper?
items.e: Shop A: 15% of $1800 = $270 off, so $1530, and $1530 + $137.70 GST = $1667.70. Shop B: $1550, and $1550 + $139.50 GST = $1689.50. Difference: $1689.50 − $1667.70 = $21.80. Shop A is cheaper by $21.80. ($20 is the difference before GST.)
